summary: Sleeping Beauty rock-top lookout cab, built about 1930-31 and gone after 1966; footings and eye bolts remain, reached by a hikers-only Forest Service trail.

facts.status_note: Removed a few years after 1966 per FFLOS and WillhiteWeb; firelookout.com says destroyed. Footings and a foundation remain per WillhiteWeb photo captions.

staffing.status: Don Williams named as the first lookout; no later lookouts named in the sources read

access.note: Forest Service trail open to hikers only; closed to all motorized use and bicycles

visit.trail_note: FS Trail #37 is 1.4 miles and very steep; WillhiteWeb lists 1.5 miles and 1,400 feet of gain. Directions: west about a mile from Trout Lake to Road 88, then north on 88 for 7 miles.

events.note: Around 1930 per WillhiteWeb and Washington Forest Lookouts; FFLOS and firelookout.com say 1931
Apparently still in use in 1966 per FFLOS; WillhiteWeb says it is said to have been in use then
Removed a few years after 1966; 1966 is a placeholder since no exact year is given. firelookout.com says destroyed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: WillhiteWeb and Washington Forest Lookouts say around 1930; FFLOS and firelookout.com say 1931. The story gives both years.
FFLOS and WillhiteWeb say removed a few years after 1966; firelookout.com says destroyed. The story reports both.
The Forest Service gives the trail as 1.4 miles; WillhiteWeb gives 1.5 miles. Both are shown.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height_m 4.3 is not in any source read, so it is left out of facts; please check it before publishing. The record's elevation 1495.7 m matches FFLOS 4,907 ft (1,496 m). A 1931 newspaper quoted by WillhiteWeb puts a working camp at the base of the nose at 4,200 feet, a different point from the summit, so it is not a conflict. Built year is 1930 or 1931 depending on source. Staffing is one named lookout, undated.
